headline: Cupid, HFCL, Sterlite Tech and MTAR among 10 stocks delivering over 150% returns in Samvat 2082
hook: Ten multibaggers delivered over 150% in Samvat 2082
summary: Ten Indian equities recorded gains exceeding 150% over the course of Samvat 2082 leading up to Diwali. The list includes prominent names such as Cupid, HFCL, Sterlite Technologies, and MTAR Technologies. These stocks outperformed broader market indices during the Samvat period. Retail investors tracking past multibagger performance can review historical returns for portfolio insights.
why_it_matters: Review past performance trends of high-flying Samvat stocks
winners_losers: Samvat 2082 multibagger holders gain / trailing stocks lag

headline: Ten multibagger stocks soared over 150% in Samvat 2082
hook: Sixteen Nifty 500 stocks doubled despite broader falls
summary: Indian equities fell during Samvat 2082 due to foreign outflows, geopolitical tensions, and higher crude oil prices. Despite the market downturn, 16 Nifty 500 stocks managed to gain more than 100%. Cupid and Sterlite Technologies led the pack with stellar returns of 570% and 556% respectively. Other notable multibaggers included HFCL and MTAR Technologies.
why_it_matters: Identifies outlier stocks that outperformed during a tough year
winners_losers: Multibagger stock holders gain / broader market hurt

headline: MTAR Tech, Netweb Tech, and three other Nifty 500 stocks dip below RSI 30
hook: Oversold territory for select Nifty 500 stocks
summary: Five stocks within the Nifty 500 index, including MTAR Technologies and Netweb Technologies, have dropped below the Relative Strength Index (RSI) threshold of 30. An RSI reading below 30 typically indicates that a security is in oversold territory based on recent price momentum. Technical analysts monitor this level to identify potential reversal points or prolonged downtrends. Retail investors holding these counters should review their fundamental thesis before making addition or exit decisions.
why_it_matters: Oversold technical levels may signal a rebound or deeper correction.

headline: Sterlite Technologies, HFCL, and MTAR Technologies hit 5% lower circuits
hook: AI stocks hit hard in sharp selloff
summary: Sterlite Technologies and HFCL shares dropped by 5% to hit lower circuits, trading at Rs 719.15 and Rs 209.95 respectively. MTAR Technologies also fell by 5% alongside a broader decline across several artificial intelligence-themed stocks. Such sharp circuit-limit drops restrict trading liquidity and signal sudden selling pressure for retail investors holding these counters.
why_it_matters: Sudden lower circuits trap retail capital and halt selling options.

headline: Analysts highlight five private defence stocks amid sector localisation push
hook: Private defence firms join HAL and BEL
summary: Market analysts are drawing attention to five private-sector defence companies alongside established public-sector firms like HAL and BEL. The featured stocks include MTAR Technologies, Zen Technologies, Astra Microwave, Data Patterns, and Apollo Micro Systems. This focus stems from India's ongoing domestic defence localisation push. Retail investors tracking the defence sector should note the broadening analyst coverage beyond public PSUs.
why_it_matters: Private defence suppliers see broader analyst attention.
winners_losers: Private defence stocks gain / PSU monopolies face competition

headline: Telecom and tech hardware stocks hit 5% lower circuits
hook: Sharp pullback on massive year-to-date gains
summary: Shares of HFCL, MTAR Technologies, and Sterlite Technologies dropped to their 5% lower circuits following a market correction. Despite this pullback, all three counters have delivered massive multi-bagger returns in calendar year 2026 so far. STL is up 664%, MTAR has gained 171%, and HFCL is higher by 151%. These sharp moves come against the backdrop of an 11.6% decline in the BSE Sensex during the same period. Retail investors holding these high-flying stocks should prepare for heightened volatility after an outsized run-up.
why_it_matters: High-flying tech stocks face sudden profit-booking and volatility
